aiOverview.content: On April 1, 2026, NASA launched the Artemis II mission, sending four astronauts on a 10-day,8-hour journey around the Moon and back. This historic mission, the first crewed lunar flight since 1972, includes NASA’s Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency’s Jeremy Hansen. This video shows the historic launch of the Artemis II mission:05:54CBS Evening NewsYouTube• Apr 1, 2026 05:54 Mission Details and Crew Mission Goal: To test NASA's Orion capsule and Space Launch System (SLS) rocket to prepare for future long-term human presence on the Moon. The Crew: Reid Wiseman (NASA): Commander. Victor Glover (NASA): Pilot. Christina Hammock Koch (NASA): Mission Specialist. Jeremy Hansen (Canadian Space Agency): Mission Specialist. Flight Path: The crew will travel over 695,000 miles (1,118,000 km) on a round trip, with no landing on the surface planned. Key Moments: The mission involves an "automated backflip" test of the spacecraft, where the crew will rely on visual inspection to verify the proximity to the upper stage rocket, with pilot Victor Glover taking control. Key Takeaways First Crewed Moon Mission in >50 Years: Artemis II is the first human mission to leave Earth orbit toward the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972. Testing Technology: This mission is a crucial stepping stone toward a planned lunar landing in 2028. Astronauts' Life: The crew will share a 60-minute mealtime daily and sleep for eight hours simultaneously, utilizing specialized storage and heating techniques for their meals.
